description: Mineral Commodity Summaries is the annual report of the U.S. Geological Survey's National Minerals Information Center and the earliest government publication of estimates for the nonfuel mineral industry. The 2026 edition (version 1.3, May 2026, 222 pages) gives two-page synopses for more than 90 minerals and materials, each with events, trends and issues, domestic industry structure, government programmes, tariffs, five-year salient statistics, and world mine production, reserves and resources by country; it is the earliest complete source of 2025 world mineral production. Appendices define units, terms and the reserve and resource classification and list USGS country specialists. The report is a free PDF with a companion data release of machine-readable tables and a data visualisation, and editions go back many years; as a U.S. Government work it is in the public domain. Caveats: world figures are country totals estimated from many sources and revised in later editions, and reserves follow national reporting practices that differ. For simulation it gives production, reserve and import-reliance figures for supply-chain, concentration-risk and capacity-planning analyses of critical minerals. Related catalogue records include World Mining Data from the Austrian ministry and the USGS Mineral Resources Data System.
